title: String and &str
summary: String owns and grows; &str is borrowed text; methods flow between them.
lecture: Rust has two everyday text types. `String` owns its text and can grow; `&str` is borrowed text - every literal like `"ferris"` is a `&str`. Functions that only read text take `&str`; functions that produce new text return `String`.
Methods move between the two: `to_string()` and `to_uppercase()` produce owned `String`s; `trim()` returns a `&str` view of the same text. Chains type-check step by step, so the order matters.
Growing text in place uses `push_str` on a `mut String`. The `+` operator also concatenates, but it consumes the left side - the ownership decks explain exactly why.

example.code:
let cleaned = raw.trim();           // &str view
let owned = cleaned.to_string();    // owned copy
example.caption: trim borrows; to_string allocates.
